knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 3 \\ -2\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-3 \\ -8 \\ 6\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ -3\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 3 x_{1} \\ - 2 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- 3 x_{2} \\ - 8 x_{2} \\ 6 x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=1 \\ 3 x_{1} - 8 x_{2} + 5 x_{3} &=-1 \\ - 2 x_{1} + 6 x_{2} - 3 x_{3} &=4\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -8 & 5 & -1 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ -2 & 6 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 6\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(2)R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - 3 x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=1 \\ x_{2} - x_{3} &=-4 \\ x_{3} &=6\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=6.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(-1)(6)=-4\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=2
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-3)(2)+(2)(6)=1\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=-5
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=-5$, $x_2=2$, $x_3=6$, which means

$$
-5a_1+(2)a_2+(6)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(-5)+(2)+(6)=3.
$$

knowledge_point.title: Solving for Three Coefficients in a Linear Combination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the vectors

$$
a_1=\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix},\quad a_2=\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix},\quad a_3=\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad b=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -35 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}
$$

If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b,$ then what is $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
If $x_1a_1+x_2a_2+x_3a_3=b$, then we have

$$
\begin{aligned}x_1\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{bmatrix}+x_2\begin{bmatrix}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}+x_3\begin{bmatrix}2 \\ 5 \\ 1\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -35 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} \\ 0 \\ 3 x_{1}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}- x_{2} \\ 0 \\ - x_{2}\end{bmatrix}+\begin{bmatrix}2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -35 \\ 5\end{bmatrix} \\ \begin{bmatrix}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} \\ 5 x_{3} \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3}\end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix}-14 \\ -35 \\ 5\end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

Equating the corresponding components, we get the following system:

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=-14 \\ 5 x_{3} &=-35 \\ 3 x_{1} - x_{2} + x_{3} &=5\end{aligned}\right.
$$

We will solve this system using Gaussian elimination. First, we write the augmented matrix for this system:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -35 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right]
$$

Row-reducing the augmented matrix, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}M&=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -35 \\ 3 & -1 & 1 & 5\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -35 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 47\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-3)R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 2 & -5 & 47 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -35\end{array}\right] && R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & \frac{47}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & -35\end{array}\right] && R_{2}:=(\frac{1}{2})R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 2 & -14 \\ 0 & 1 & - \frac{5}{2} & \frac{47}{2} \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -7\end{array}\right] && R_{3}:=(\frac{1}{5})R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x_{1} - x_{2} + 2 x_{3} &=-14 \\ x_{2} - \frac{5 x_{3}}{2} &=\frac{47}{2} \\ x_{3} &=-7\end{aligned}\right.
$$

From the third equation, we get $x_3=-7.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
1x_2+(- \frac{5}{2})(-7)=\frac{47}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_2=6
$$

Finally, substituting these values into the first equation, we obtain

$$
x_1+(-1)(6)+(2)(-7)=-14\quad\Rightarrow\quad x_1=6
$$

So, the solution of the system is $x_1=6$, $x_2=6$, $x_3=-7$, which means

$$
6a_1+(6)a_2+(-7)a_3=b.
$$

Consequently,

$$
x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3}=(6)+(6)+(-7)=5.
$$
